name: Coordinated Inauthentic Behavior
description: Detection and analysis of coordinated link-sharing and inauthentic networks on social media platforms, including the CooRnet/CLSB methodology, the VERA-AI Alert monitoring system, and case studies of deceptive information operations. This is the researcher's signature methodological contribution and remains the most active strand of his agenda.

name: Platform Governance and Researcher Data Access
description: Study of how social media platforms regulate, restrict, or structure access to data for independent research, including Meta's political content reduction policies, the CrowdTangle shutdown's effect on methods, the Digital Services Act's researcher-access provisions, and critiques of API/data-sharing regimes.

name: Generative AI and Synthetic Media Manipulation
description: Research on how generative AI is reshaping disinformation and persuasion, from AI-generated visual propaganda and gambling promotion to the use of LLMs as annotation and classification tools in computational social science, and broader theorizing of the emerging 'AI society'.

name: Political Polarization and Partisan Media Dynamics
description: Analysis of affective polarization, partisan community dynamics, and the interplay between social and traditional media in amplifying political extremes, spanning Italian, Brazilian, and comparative international contexts.

name: Social Media and Electoral Campaigns
description: Empirical studies of political communication and citizen engagement on Facebook/Instagram around specific elections (Italy 2018/2022, Germany 2021, Brazil post-Bolsonaro), tracking news circulation, advertising, and coordinated campaign activity.

name: Health Misinformation and Problematic Content Networks
description: Mapping of coordinated networks and alternative influence structures spreading problematic health information, including COVID-19 fact-checking acceleration tools and country-specific studies in India and Nigeria.

name: Computational and LLM-Assisted Content Analysis
description: Methodological work on applying large language models and embedding techniques to classify and annotate political and news text at scale, including validation challenges of LLM-in-the-loop pipelines for communication research.

name: Information Disorder and Fake News Conceptualization
description: Foundational and ongoing theoretical work defining and taxonomizing misleading information within the hybrid media system, underpinning the researcher's broader disinformation research program.

name: Digital and Social Media Research Methods
description: Development and critique of data collection and research infrastructure for studying digital platforms, including survey recruitment via Facebook ads, APIs and tools assessment in the DSA era, and ethical/interdisciplinary considerations in computational social science.

name: Platforms, Audiences, and Online Communities
description: Empirical and reflective studies of how platform affordances, cultures, and audience practices shape online sociality, identity, and community formation across sites like Facebook, TikTok, Instagram, Twitter/Mastodon, and LiveJournal.

name: Critical Analysis of AI Industry Imaginaries and Discourse
description: Studies examining how AI industry actors, media, and communities construct and circulate narratives, imaginaries, and framings (e.g., longtermism, techno-hagiography, 'quiet futuring', political-economy 'decoys') that shape public understanding and obscure or legitimize the underlying power structures of AI development.

name: Reflections on the State of Misinformation and Online Harm Research
description: Papers that step back from primary empirical study to critically assess the misinformation/online-harms research field itself — diagnosing biases (e.g., WEIRD-centrism, overreliance on cognitive proxies), mapping gaps in evidence (causal, longitudinal, cross-national), and proposing directions or borrowed lessons (e.g., from climate psychology) to make the field more rigorous and generalizable.

name: Theorizing AI's Social Role: Agency, Trust, and Public Perception
description: Papers that apply or extend social theory and communication-trust frameworks to understand the societal position of AI systems, ranging from conceptual demarcations of machine agency and formal multi-agent social frameworks to models of public trust in generative AI and empirical survey data on public attitudes toward AI adoption.

name: Computational Studies of Political Media and Advertising
description: Papers using large-scale computational or quasi-experimental methods to study political advertising, media capture, and ideological signaling on digital platforms, including causal analysis of ad effects, detection of covert advertiser influence on news coverage, and latent ideology estimation of political video content.

name: Survey Measurement Validity and Comparability
description: Papers examining methodological challenges in survey-based measurement, including whether respondents understand survey questions as intended, how online sample composition and quality checks affect representativeness and response validity, and how question wording and dataset differences affect cross-national and longitudinal comparability of trust measures.
